plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between 0 and 49, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To win with high probability, and minimize overpayment, I will bid slightly above this. A bid of $33.00 seems reasonable.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your value minus a small increment. In a two-player scenario, bidding slightly above the second highest value is optimal. However, with three players, the risk of overpaying increases. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid slightly below my value to encourage others to bid and reveal their valuations. I choose a bid of $26.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is (2/3) * 49 = 32.67. To maximize profit, bid slightly above this, but considering my own value of $13, I should bid conservatively. Bidding too high risks paying more than the item is worth to me.
